src-aug-2025-resume-networking-training.summary: This session advises looking for repeated words in job descriptions and incorporating them into resume bullets to match the role's language.
details: Look for repeated words in a target job description and try to repeat those in your resume bullets
If the posting says “The successful candidate must commit to XYZ dates,” be ready to commit to these

Really long phrases (bullets that are extra long or at a greater level of detail than the others) suggest this is a pain point in the company; network to confirm this is the case and emphasize the skills that can “fix” or combat this
Most job descriptions are templates that hiring managers then tweak for the most important aspects of the role
If there is a phrase that is a-typical, it means it was intentionally changed

src-aug-2025-resume-networking-training.summary: The recommended resume formats depend on the intended next move, focusing on readability for recruiters who spend only 7-8 seconds per resume.
details: Chronological format is for classic/traditional industries or single pivots
Hybrid format places job titles all in a row under the company name with sections of bullets under function or skill
Functional format is most rated for big pivots, unfamiliar industries, transferable skills, or when the whole career is in one industry
Remove undergrad GPA because it opens you up to comparison
Remove undergrad awards unless you have space
Make sure you have an additional humorous section to entice the reader to ask about it

src-aug-2025-resume-networking-training.summary: Resume bullets should include at least three elements: What, How, and Impact, and should be explicit rather than mysterious.
details: Resume bullets should include 3/4 elements at a minimum: What (the thing/work object), How (skills used), and Impact (measurable outcome ideally)
Start with “impact” if it is large; start with “how” if you are pivoting industry or role
All bullets should be explicit rather than intentionally mysterious to generate curiosity or a follow-up question
Adjectives and adverbs make a bullet long
Use abbreviations only if you are moving within the same industry or function

src-aug-2025-resume-only-workshop.summary: Resume bullets should include at least three elements: What, How, and Impact. The starting point for a bullet depends on whether you are emphasizing impact, how, or pivoting.
details: Resume bullets should include 3/4 elements at a minimum
What: The thing, or “work object,” you made
How: What skills you used to make that work object (skills should be tailored to the employer/role)
Impact: Measurable outcome ideally
Why: Why was it important, was it part of a company’s bigger strategy? How often did you do it, etc.
